source: actual B3 Linux dry-run wall-clock measurements (dryrun_2026-09-23.json)

setup_vs_execution.note: wall_s includes per-container venv creation + commit dependency install (network-bound) + 3x target + 3x parent per-file runs + junit parsing. Era image builds (~2-5 min each) and cache copy (~1-2 min) are one-time and amortized; postgres start ~10s.
setup_vs_execution.one_time_setup_s: era builds ~150-300s each (3 images); cache copy ~60-120s; postgres ~10s

cache_warm_vs_cold.observation: repeated task reruns did not warm deps (containers are --rm; uv cache per-container), but failed-run reruns dropped from 579s to 218s once postgres was healthy - the drop is defect-removal, not cache warming
cache_warm_vs_cold.conclusion: treat every task as cache-cold for deps; pip install dominates for small test sets

c2_main_220_projection.basis: 220 x [median 751s .. p90 1024s]; min realistic small-task 218s; MAIN 220 are predominantly MODIFIED with 1-3 changed test files
c2_main_220_projection.chunking: resumable; worktrees persist on Linux ext4; per-task JSON records support resume

c4_dev_projection.basis: DEV census: 111/150 tasks have changed-test evidence; 111 x [median 751s .. p90 1024s]

parallelism.reason: mission resource rule forbids parallel heavy commands; shared postgres with Django test-DB creation/migrations would contend; 13GB RAM supports 1-2 concurrent but DB isolation per-state already implemented; conservative sequential is the frozen scientific-safe choice
